Identify the differential equation that generated the slope field above.
worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14045300/assets/78f281b8039a5897ca8013324c676095b6e1f57278cbab35b05c5eb3b4360301.png)

 

Notice the following properties of the given slope field:

- First, the slopes become horizontal along the lines $y=\pm x.$

Of the given equations, the only equations that satisfy this condition are the following:

$$
\begin{aligned} & {y}^{′}=\frac{2({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})}{{y}^{2}} \\  & {y}^{′}={y}^{2}-{x}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

- Second, for $x\ne 0,$ the slopes become vertical as $y\to 0.$ 

Of the remaining options, the only one that gives this behavior is

$$
{y}^{′}=\frac{2({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})}{{y}^{2}}.
$$

For $x\ne 0,$ notice that

$$
|{y}^{′}|=|\frac{2({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})}{{y}^{2}}|\to \infty \,\text{as}\,y\to 0.
$$

Therefore, the slopes of the slope field for the differential equation ${y}^{′}=\frac{2({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})}{{y}^{2}}$ become vertical as $y\to 0.$
By contrast, 

$$
{y}^{′}={y}^{2}-{x}^{2}\to -{x}^{2}\,\text{as}\,y\to 0.
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is

$$
{y}^{′}=\frac{2({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})}{{y}^{2}}.
$$
